sources.entry: GoToSocial - ActivityPub federated social network server implementing the Mastodon client API. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker/Go

summary.name: GoToSocial
summary.one_liner: GoToSocial is a lightweight, Go-written ActivityPub social network server that implements the Mastodon client API, currently in beta.
use_cases: run a personal or small community social server
federate with Mastodon and other fediverse servers
use Mastodon client apps with a self-hosted server
host a low-resource social instance on a Raspberry Pi or cheap VPS
social media without algorithmic timelines or tracking
summary.what_it_does: GoToSocial is an ActivityPub server written in Go that lets users follow, post, reply, favourite and share, with a chronological timeline and no recommendation algorithm. It implements and extends the Mastodon API so existing Mastodon-compatible apps can be used. Posts support public, unlisted, followers-only and direct visibility, Markdown formatting, local-only posting, and an opt-in RSS feed. Admins can run federation in blocklist or allowlist modes, and it supports OIDC identity providers and two-factor authentication. It is distributed as a binary, a Docker image, or built from source, and uses SQLite or an external database.
notable: Implements and extends the Mastodon client API, so many Mastodon apps work
Lightweight: about 250-350MiB RAM, runs on single-board computers and small VPSes
Backend-only: no bundled web client front-end; designed for third-party front-ends
Chronological timelines with no recommendation algorithm
caveats: Still beta software with many bugs and unimplemented features; beta exit expected around 2026
Zero federation mode is not yet implemented
Not officially supported on 32-bit systems or OpenBSD; performance may suffer
Local-only posting depends on client support
